rv.q: Midnight already sounds, looks, and innovates like the best new musical of the year.
But there's no denying someone else should have looked at all these elements, which might have made "Midnight" a more satisfying (and shorter) event.
Subtlety, and even humor, is in short supply, the show being staged with such perpetual drive that, for all its pyrotechnics, it too rarely touches your heart.
By the end you may find yourself in complete awe at the talent you’ve witnessed onstage and the genuine brilliance that Hall possesses in mind, body, and vocal cords.
But put together in context, these components create a strange, complex experience that’s not exactly unenjoyable, but somewhat dubious.

The trouble is that much of “Midnight” feels like just that, a showcase, both for Mr. Hall’s ideals and for the undeniably impressive gifts of his fellow actors, rather than a terribly compelling or even truly provocative story.
Todrick Hall's Midnight at the Theatre is the best musical I've seen since Hamilton.
Todrick Hall’s Midnight wears its message in every lyric, and with voices this powerful carrying it, a few hours in someone else’s shoes is time well spent.
Todrick Hall’s Midnight is the bold, completely original theatrical adventure I have hungered for in Broadway’s recent years.
Currently playing at the Theatre, it is, hands down, the best new musical I have seen this season.
Todrick Hall was given the opportunity to create his own unique vision on stage, and to quote his fellow artistic traveler, he did not throw away his shot.
This is Midnight, an ambitious sucker punch of emotion overflowing with surprises and some of the most outstanding vocals I've ever heard either on or off Broadway.

cn.t: Critics praise Hall's ambitious multi-hyphenate achievement in "Midnight," highlighting its effective choreography, catchy music, and innovative theatrical storytelling that explores race and identity through a Civil War-era lens.
